conventions.convention: Alphabets are finite and nonempty; zero coordinates remain in the alphabet. P ≪ Q means supp P ⊆ supp Q.

A generator is finite and convex on (0,∞), with f(1)=0. Positive Q-mass at zero P-mass uses f(0); positive P-mass at zero Q-mass uses the recession value f∞. Jointly zero coordinates contribute zero, and a zero singular coefficient contributes zero even when f∞=+∞.
P is the null and Q is the alternative. The test function is rejection probability; βε(P,Q) minimizes acceptance under Q subject to rejection under P being at most ε.
K(y|x) is nonnegative and sums to one over y for each input x; (PK)y = Σx px K(y|x).
KL is directed from its first law to its second, uses natural logarithms, assigns zero to zero P-mass, and is +∞ whenever P is not absolutely continuous with respect to Q.

Rényi orders are positive. At order one the divergence is KL. Singular P-mass contributes zero affinity below order one and infinite affinity above order one; zero affinity below order one gives infinite divergence. Division by α−1 reverses inequalities below order one.
The testing exponent uses integer blocklengths n≥1, fixed ε∈(0,1), and −log 0 := +∞.

load_bearing.statement: Let f:(0,∞)→R be convex and satisfy f(1)=0. Then f is continuous on (0,∞), and both extended-real limits f(0):=lim(t↓0) f(t) and f∞:=lim(t→∞) f(t)/t exist in R∪{+∞}; neither limit is −∞.
Let f be a convex generator from def-finite-f-divergence, with its stated closed perspective Πf on nonnegative pairs. For every finite family (ai,bi)∈[0,∞)², Πf(Σi ai,Σi bi) ≤ Σi Πf(ai,bi).

Let P,Q be probability vectors on a finite nonempty alphabet X, let K be a stochastic kernel from X to a finite nonempty alphabet Y, and let f be a convex generator as in def-finite-f-divergence. Then Df(PK||QK) ≤ Df(P||Q), with both divergences interpreted using that definition's zero and singular-support conventions.
For f(t)=t log t on t>0, one has f(1)=0, f is convex on (0,∞), lim(t↓0) f(t)=0, and lim(t→∞) f(t)/t=+∞.

For α>1, hα(t)=t^α−1 is convex on (0,∞), satisfies hα(1)=0, has hα(0+)=−1, and has recession limit +∞. For 0<α<1, gα(t)=1−t^α is convex on (0,∞), satisfies gα(1)=0, has gα(0+)=1, and has recession limit 0.

For finite probability vectors P ≪ Q and independent Xi with common law P, define ℓ(x)=log(px/qx) when px>0 and ℓ(x)=0 otherwise, and Ln=Σi=1ⁿ ℓ(Xi). Then Ln/n→D(P||Q) in probability. For every xⁿ∈supp(P)ⁿ, Qⁿ(xⁿ)=Pⁿ(xⁿ) exp(−Ln(xⁿ)).
